theme.title: The dynasty years
theme.subtitle: Chicago Bulls, 1991–98
theme.recap: Chicago won 69 games a year after 72, buried Utah by 42 in a Finals game and then fell to 13 wins once the team broke up.

questions.prompt: How many points did Michael Jordan score in Game 4 of the 1993 Finals against Phoenix?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: In Game 4, Michael Jordan was unstoppable, scoring 55 points at Chicago Stadium

funFacts.text: Jordan faced reigning league MVP Charles Barkley, who had lifted the Suns to the league's best record.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: winners of 62 games and led by regular season MVP Charles Barkley

funFacts.text: Scott Williams joked that he and fellow North Carolina alumnus Jordan had combined for an absurd scoring total.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Scott Williams, who like MJ played his college basketball at UNC

funFacts.text: Earlier in the series, Phoenix had won a marathon triple-overtime game at Chicago Stadium.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Phoenix Suns won Game 3 in triple overtime

questions.prompt: How many games did the 1996–97 Bulls win, a year after going 72–10?
questions.note: 69–13, the league's best record that season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Bulls settled for a league-best 69–13 record

funFacts.text: Chicago began the season with an undefeated opening stretch, looking ready to repeat its previous dominance.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: They began the season 12–0

funFacts.text: Late-season injuries and a last-game missed shot by Scottie Pippen stopped the Bulls' record chase.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Scottie Pippen's failed attempt at a game-winning three-pointer

funFacts.text: Utah's first Finals appearance came with a bold mountain-themed rebrand of its uniforms and logo.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: a bold, gradient "Purple Mountain" motif

questions.prompt: Utah lost Game 3 of the 1998 Finals by 42 points. How many points did the Jazz score?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: In a 96–54 loss, the Jazz set the record for the 42-point loss in Finals history

funFacts.text: Chicago's entire roster eventually scored in the rout, including backup center Bill Wennington late.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Every player on the Bulls roster scored at least once

funFacts.text: Utah had beaten Chicago in both regular-season meetings and entered the championship series confident.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Jazz had won both regular season meetings with the Bulls

funFacts.text: The Jazz entered the Finals after sweeping Shaquille O'Neal's Los Angeles Lakers in the West finals.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Jazz uneventfully swept the Los Angeles Lakers

questions.prompt: Scottie Pippen tied the Finals record for threes in Game 3 of 1997. How many did he make?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Scottie Pippen tying a then-Finals record with seven 3-pointers

funFacts.text: Pippen's long-range clinic still came in a loss because Karl Malone dominated the interior for Utah.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Utah was led by Karl Malone, who scored 37 points and had 10 rebounds

funFacts.text: The Salt Lake City crowd was so loud that Bulls players covered their ears during the introductions.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Bulls players plugged their ears, due to the loud cheers and fireworks

funFacts.text: Chicago nearly erased a big late deficit, but Utah earned its first win of the series.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Chicago attempted a 4th-quarter comeback, cutting a 24-point deficit down to 7

questions.prompt: In the lockout season after their sixth title, how many games did the Bulls win?
questions.note: 13, in the lockout-shortened season after their sixth title.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: winning just 13 of 50 games

funFacts.text: Jordan's retirement and departures of Pippen and Rodman broke up the Bulls dynasty after the second three-peat.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Dennis Rodman (who signed with the Los Angeles Lakers as a free agent), and Jordan's second retirement

funFacts.text: Tim Floyd replaced Phil Jackson on the Chicago bench and inherited a team that lost most of its opening games.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Under Floyd, and with the addition of Barry and Bryant, the Bulls were a shell of their former selves

funFacts.text: Toni Kukoč became Chicago's leading scorer in the first post-dynasty season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Toni Kukoč became the team's scoring leader
